title: Three bands of light
caption: Zodiacal light, airglow and the Milky Way, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Three bands of light share this sky, and a lone figure stands at the centre watching them: ESO Photo Ambassador Babak Tafreshi, during ESO's UHD Expedition. The first band is the faint glow reaching up from the horizon just below the middle of the frame. This is zodiacal light, sunlight scattered by cosmic dust lying in the plane of Earth's orbit.

The second, red band hugs the horizon at lower left. It is airglow, light from Earth's own upper atmosphere, driven by several processes: cosmic rays, photoionised atoms recombining, and chemical reactions involving oxygen, nitrogen, hydroxyl, sodium and lithium.

The third band, high overhead, is the Milky Way, our home galaxy, made of billions of stars of every kind. Thick layers of interstellar dust hide many of them from the human eye and give the band its familiar mottled look.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph credited to ESO/B. Tafreshi; the packet does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: Zodiacal light and airglow are faint, and a camera gathering light over time may show them, especially the airglow's red colour, more clearly than the eye.

alt: A person standing beneath the night sky, with a faint glow rising from the horizon, a red glow at lower left and the Milky Way high above.
